learning_outcomes.text: Has ordered and deepened knowledge of methods for measuring non-electrical quantities in industry.
Knows and understands issues related to the principle of operation and correct application of measurement methods and sensors.
Has knowledge enabling understanding of new measurement methods and the principle of operation of new designs of measurement sensors.
Can use the learned operating methods of measurement systems and sensors for planning and conducting measurement experiments.
Can process measurement results and apply analytical and experimental methods to analyze and evaluate the accuracy of sensors and measurement paths.
Can compare design variants of measurement systems and designs of measurement sensors in terms of given operational and economic criteria.
Has the ability to work in a team and awareness of responsibility for one's own work and joint activities during the implementation of measurement experiments.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to industrial measurements of non-electrical quantities. Structure and physical principles of non-electrical quantity sensor construction. Structure of the measurement path and static and dynamic properties of measurement path components. Industrial measurement conditions.

Measurements of mechanical quantities part I – solids. Methods for measuring mechanical parameters in drive systems: torque, rotational speed, mechanical power. Measurements of forces, mass, moments of force. Measurements of displacement, speed, and acceleration. Measurements of vibration parameters and paraseismic vibrations.

Measurements of mechanical quantities part II – fluids. Methods for measuring pressures, absolute and differential pressure. Measurements of fluid flow, determination of mass and volumetric flow rate, flow velocity, fluid meters. Basic flow transducers. Methods for measuring liquid level, continuous measurement, level indicators.

Temperature measurements, thermodynamic and thermal measurements. Contact temperature transducers: resistive, thermoelectric, semiconductor. Measurement methods and systems. Non-contact temperature transducers, pyrometers and thermal imaging cameras. Measurements of thermodynamic parameters (measurement of instantaneous values of pressure, temperature, and volume, determination of the thermodynamic cycle). Measurements of thermal power and energy in a heating system (physical principles of measurement, measurement of thermal power and energy transferred by liquid, efficiency of the heating system).

Measurements of physical and physicochemical properties of substances. Measurements of chemical composition. Methods for measuring humidity of gases and solids. Measurement of viscosity and density of fluids. Determination of hydrogen ion concentration PH. Measurements of chemical composition using radiation - spectrometry. Gas and liquid chromatography.

Acoustic measurements. Properties of the acoustic field. Concepts of sound pressure and sound pressure level, sound intensity and sound intensity level, loudness. Types and properties of microphones. Measurements of noise and acoustic quantities.

Optical and illumination measurements. Laser methods for measuring distance and displacement: time-of-flight, triangulation, and interferometric methods. Rangefinders. Fiber optic transducers for measuring non-electrical quantities. Measurements of illumination intensity, photometric transducer.
Overview of applications of non-electrical measurements in industry. Utility measurements in the automotive, food, aviation, sports, construction, medicine, meteorology industries.
Introduction to the laboratory, substantive discussion of exercises, OHS regulations, credit conditions.
Application of tensometric methods in industrial measurements.
Configuring and testing the properties of an industrial system for measuring thermal energy consumption.
Determining the properties of paths for measuring mechanical vibration parameters.
Measurements of mechanical parameters of drive systems.
Investigation of metrological properties of temperature sensors.
Determining metrological characteristics of a digital angle sensor and acceleration sensors.
Measurements of air humidity and temperature control using the P18D transducer and calibration of integrated pressure sensors.
assessment_rules: Lectures are assessed by an examination. Laboratory classes are assessed based on activity during classes, execution of laboratory classes, tests, reports, and involvement in teamwork. Students must prepare for laboratory exercises, which may be verified by an oral or written colloquium. Credit for the module is possible after crediting all laboratory classes.
